title: Isolate small-request floods to prevent long-context tail latency across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Summary:
Several customers (Hosted production tenants and two Dedicated clusters) reported intermittent severe tail latency for long-context requests during peak small-request traffic. The observed pattern: a sustained flood of short, low-token requests causes the continuous-batching scheduler to prefer small batches and evict or delay long-context streams, which in turn reduces KV cache residency for long-running sessions and produces long-context tail latency spikes.

Scope / Impact:
- Affects Hosted API (multi-tenant routing) and Dedicated clusters with mixed workloads. One Private deployment reported similar symptoms after enabling mixed-size endpoints.
- Customer impact: request timeouts and user-facing slowdowns for features that rely on long-context prompts (document assistants, chat history resumptions).
- Severity: high (customer escalations opened by two enterprise customers; potential SLA breaches).

Reproduction steps (local + prod verification):
1) Start a mixed workload generator that issues 8k qps of 16-token requests interleaved with 50 rps long-context (8k tokens) requests to the same model variant.
2) Observe continuous-batching scheduler log traces: large number of small batch flushes, eviction of in-flight long-request KV caches, and increased preemption of long-streams.
3) Correlate with per-stream cache metrics: KV cache miss rates jump for long-context streams concurrent with small-request flood.
4) Reproduce in Dedicated using the customer's config and in Hosted by re-playing sampling of production traffic in canary pool.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- Scheduler fairness heuristic uses aggregated throughput / latency score that unintentionally biases short requests under certain arrival distributions (burst of small requests with low token counts).
- Continuous batching logic aggressively prioritizes batch completion over preserving KV cache locality; when a small-request flood occurs, long-context sessions lose cache locality and suffer longer generation times due to cache rehydration and cold-kernel paths.
- On Dedicated/Private, affinity rules were weaker for multi-tenant pools that host mixed-size routes, allowing interleaving across model replicas.

Proposed fix (design):
1) Short-term mitigation (hotfix, immediate rollout):
   - Introduce an isolation queue for tiny/fast requests per node/pool that caps the fraction of GPU time they can consume (configurable cap, default 20%).
   - Add a heuristic to the scheduler to reduce preemption of streams with >2048 token KV caches (preserve active KV residency).
   - Deploy rate-limited admission for non-critical small requests in Hosted (customer-configurable via API route label).
2) Medium-term (next runtime release):
   - Scheduler fairness rewrite to include per-stream "cache residency score" + arrival-size-aware aging to prevent starvation of long streams.
   - Stronger replica affinity: pin long-context sessions to a smaller set of replicas to preserve KV cache, while short requests are spread across a larger pool.
3) Long-term: kernel-level optimizations to speed cache rehydration and reduce cold-path penalty to lower the cost of eviction when unavoidable.

Rollout plan per deployment mode:
- Hosted: Emergency config push to canary region (us-west-2) today with isolation queue enabled for non-critical routes. Monitor tail latency and KV cache hit-rate for 12h. If stable, promote to global rollout over 48h with telemetry gating.
- Dedicated: Provide C1 patch to tenant clusters — engage SE to coordinate maintenance windows (non-disruptive config change for most clusters). For clusters with strict isolation, recommend temporary route-level caps and offer scheduling telemetry.
- Private: Offer patch and a test harness; recommend customers run canary in isolated subnet. For air-gapped customers, provide detailed instructions and a backport if they are on older runtime.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for new scheduler heuristics and isolation queue behavior.
- Synthetic workload tests (mixed small/large arrival patterns) in CI with performance assertions on 99.9th percentile latency for long-context requests.
- End-to-end canary in Hosted with production-like traffic replay and SLO gating (if 99.9 P99.9 for long-context > baseline + 20% then abort).

Monitoring & instrumentation changes:
- Add per-stream KV cache residency metric exposed to console and internal dashboards.
- Add a new alert: sustained small-request utilization > 60% + long-context KV cache miss rate increase > 30% => Pager (P0).
- Dashboard widgets for per-pool isolation queue utilization and long-stream preemption count.

Customer communication:
- Drafted joint postmortem and mitigation email for affected customers (customer success reviewed). Temporary mitigation steps and expected timeline included.

Acceptance criteria:
- No production customer tail-latency regressions after global Hosted rollout for 72h.
- Dedicated customers confirm improved long-context 99.9th percentile within two maintenance windows.
- New metrics and alerting working and consumed by SRE/SE teams.

Follow-ups / Open questions:
- Should we make isolation-cap per-route default opt-in or opt-out for new routes? (PM input required.)
- Evaluate potential cost impact of stronger replica affinity (may increase memory footprint).
